messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TFC acceptance criteria, notice phasing, and service-transfer runbook (MSA redline)

Hi Melissa / procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our legal team's request I am circulating a concise set of asks so we can converge on language quickly:

1) Term / Auto-renew: Acme asked for a 12-month initial term with single 12-month auto-renew. Redwood's standard is auto-renew unless notice given 60 days prior. Can you confirm whether Acme is flexible on a 60-day outbound notice or needs 90 days?

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC): Acme wants a 30-day TFC right. Our ask is to preserve a 60-day operational handoff period for any TFC that triggers full service-transfer support (we can provide 30-day limited handoff but 60-day for full data/extract + runbook).

3) Notice phasing and stagger: We propose a two-tier notice ladder so smaller pilot SKUs can opt out with 30-day notice while enterprise SKUs remain on 60-day window. This avoids a hard global opt-out that breaks momentum.

4) Acceptance criteria for service transfer: See the attached svc_transfer_checklist.xlsx — the checklist defines deliverables (data export formats, runbook, access handoff, test cutover plan). We need agreement that TFC triggers the full checklist unless Acme elects the 'limited offboarding' option (reduced deliverables).

Next steps: Laura and Ben will coordinate a redline to the MSA with explicit language for TFC-triggered acceptance criteria and the two-tier notice ladder. If Acme can confirm the preferred notice windows today I can get legal to produce a narrow mark within 24 hours.

Attachments: redline_MSA_v3.docx (proposed edits), svc_transfer_checklist.xlsx

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Enterprise Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: TFC acceptance criteria, notice phasing, and service-transfer runbook (MSA redline)

Vivek / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few immediate points from legal:

- Auto-renew notice: Acme prefers 90 days for enterprise SKUs and is willing to accept 60 days for pilot/POC lines. Our procurement policy requires longer notice for large spend items.
- TFC period: Acme will not agree to a standalone 60-day 'full handoff' as a hard condition. We can accept a 60-day target for full transition support (outlined in the checklist) but need an explicit cap on Redwood's liability if we elect the limited offboarding route.
- Acceptance criteria: we propose adding a short 'mutual acceptance' step post-transfer (7-business-day verification) where both parties sign off on successful delivery of checklist items or raise exceptions.

I've attached a redline to the MSA with our suggested language (also uploaded to procurement portal). Key change is an alternative subsection that allows Acme to elect the limited offboarding; if elected, Redwood's service warranty is limited as noted.

Please advise whether Redwood can accept the mutual-acceptance step and the 90/60 split on notice windows.

Onward —
Janet Lee
Counsel, Acme Corp.
[attachment: redline_MSA_acme_comments.docx]

Subject: Re: TFC acceptance criteria, notice phasing, and service-transfer runbook (MSA redline)

Janet / Melissa —

Appreciate the quick feedback. To move this forward we are proposing the following concrete redline text (I'll drop the full mark in the doc today):

1) Notice window split: Enterprise SKUs = 90 days; Pilot/POC/Tooling SKUs = 60 days. We'll enumerate by SKU in Exhibit A.
2) TFC trigger and handoff: If Acme elects full transition support, Redwood will perform the svc_transfer_checklist within 60 calendar days of written notice; if Acme elects limited offboarding, Redwood will complete the reduced checklist within 30 calendar days and liability/warranty caps apply as per the attached redline.
3) Mutual acceptance: After transfer Redwood and Acme will enter a 7-business-day acceptance period. Any open exceptions will be documented and a remediation timeline agreed. If no exceptions are raised, the transfer is deemed accepted.
4) Escrow / data access: For added comfort, we propose a 30-day escrow window where critical runtime artifacts (export, keys metadata) are staged with a neutral escrow provider if a full handoff is requested; cost to be borne by Acme unless otherwise negotiated.

I attached an updated redline and the service checklist. If we can get confirmation on the SKU split today we will send a final mark for signature-ready review.

Attachments: redline_MSA_v4.docx (Ben's mark), svc_transfer_checklist.xlsx

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Ops (Redwood Inference)

Janet / Melissa —

Quick update from our side after review with legal and product:

- We accept the mutual acceptance step (7 business days) as redline language. We'll include a provision that exceptions raised must be actionable and tied to checklist deliverables.
- For notice windows: Redwood accepts the 90-day enterprise / 60-day pilot split provided Acme publishes SKU mapping in Exhibit A prior to signature.
- On the 60-day full transfer vs 30-day limited offboarding: we will keep both options. To protect deliverability we request an explicit election form at notice (checkboxes in the notice letter) so scope is clear.
- Escrow: product agrees to stage runtime export artifacts to an escrow provider for a 30-day window for full transfers. We will add language that Acme covers escrow costs unless the termination is for material breach by Redwood.

I'll produce the final MSA mark including the checkbox election, mutual acceptance clause, and the escrow paragraph. Expect the mark in your portal tonight. If Acme can post the SKU Exhibit A by EOD tomorrow we can keep to the timeline.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Contracts & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
